result:
I made a fix in `anthrouter/handlers.py`, but I haven't reproduced your two-turn scenario, so I'm not certain it addresses the whole bug. The full suite gives 1119 passed, 1 skipped and 1 failed. The failure is `tests/test_config.py::test_editable_fields_live_editable_fields`, which also fails on the unmodified code, so my change didn't cause it.

**Cause:** the per-conversation tier cache was keyed only by session plus a hash of the first user message. A `claude-sonnet-5-5` turn classified `trivial` wrote `haiku` into that slot. Later text-less continuation turns in the same conversation then replayed that cached tier. These are tool-result-only turns, short affirmations ("yes", "proceed"), and walk-back turns. A `claude-opus-5-5` turn picked up `haiku` this way. The replay paths skip the upgrade-only cap, and that cap wouldn't have helped anyway, because haiku ranks below opus.

**Fix:** `_prepare` now scopes the cache key by the requested model's tier (the baseline lock's tier when the lock is on). A tier cached from a sonnet-requested turn is no longer replayed onto an opus-requested one. I didn't touch the replay logic in `model_router.py`, since existing tests rely on it.

**Side effect:** a conversation that alternates requested models now keeps a separate cached tier per requested model. A continuation turn after a switch has no cached tier to replay, so it falls back to `missing_final_user_text` and keeps the requested model.

I didn't add a regression test.
